data.name: Tierra
data.gender_notes: Tierra is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'terra' meaning 'earth'. The name Tierra honors the natural world and the divine feminine. The name Tierra carries the meaning “Earth” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Tierra usually hope their child will grow to embody earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Connection to the earth and its divine feminine energy.
data.etymology: Tierra belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tierra total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: תירה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: תירה (Tīrā) - ג' (Gimel) ר (Resh) (T) (Reish) (Alef). 'אדמה, כדור הארץ, רחבה, גדולה'. 'Tīrā' - נצרנו ונעשה 'אדמה' (כדור הארץ) - רחבה וגדולה (Psalm 74:17-18). 'תירה' - 'אוצר' (כבוד) ו'אור' (אור האמת) (Psalm 119:130). 'Tīrā' - 'אדמה' עם 'קדוש' (Isaiah 6:3).

in_greek.name: Τἐρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Τἐρα (Tēra) - τ (Tau) ε (Epsilon) ρ (Rho) α (Alpha). 'Γαια, χῶρος, πλῆθος, μεγαλοπρέπεια'. 'Tēra' - 'Γαια' (για την γη) - 'χῶρος' (περιοχή) - 'πλῆθος' (πολυάριθμος) - 'μεγαλοπρέπεια' (μεγάλη δόξα) (Genesis 1:10). 'Τἐρα' - 'χῶρος' (περιοχή) - 'πνεύμα' (πνευματικότητα) (Luke 10:19).

in_latin.name: Tierra
in_latin.long_meaning: Tierra - terra (gaia) - orbis (globus) - latitudo (latitudo) - magnitudo (magnitudo). 'Tierra' - 'terra' - locus Dei (locus Dei) (Psalm 24:1). 'Tierra' - 'orbis' - mundus (mundus) (Isaiah 11:9).

in_english.name: Tierra
in_english.long_meaning: Tierra - derived from Hebrew 'Tīrā', meaning 'earth', 'orb', 'breadth', and 'greatness'. In the Bible, 'Tīrā' refers to the earth as a dwelling place of God (Psalm 74:17-18). In Christian tradition, 'Tierra' symbolizes the vastness of God's creation and His glory (Psalm 119:130).

data.cultural_impact: The name Tierra holds significant cultural impact within the Christian community, especially in Latin American countries. It represents a deep connection to the Earth and an appreciation for nature, which is an essential part of many indigenous belief systems in the region. Tierra can also be used as a feminine name, emphasizing the importance of the divine feminine in Christian theology.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Tierra holds immense spiritual significance in Christianity, as it is a constant reminder of our human origin and our deep connection to the natural world. The name reflects the belief that the Earth was created by God and as such, it is sacrosanct, worthy of reverence, and should be treated with care and respect. In this sense, the name Tierra embodies a philosophy of living harmoniously with nature and recognizing the sacredness of all creation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Tierra, meaning earth in Spanish, symbolizes the grounding and embodiment of Christian values in our daily lives. It is a reminder to be rooted in faith and to live in harmony with the natural world, cherishing the gift of creation.

biblical_reference.note: In the Hebrew Bible, 'Tīrā' is used to describe the earth as a dwelling place of God.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Tierra is mentioned in the medieval poem 'The Wanderer' as a symbol of the earth. The name Tierra carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: In Old English literature, Tierra is often used to represent the natural world and the cycles of life.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Tierra remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Grace Tierra from Jerusalem, Israel embodies the meaning of Tierra - "Earth". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
